title: Check yourself: which kind of reference, and who may build

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, what tells the compiler which kind of reference ClassName::method is, when two kinds share that syntax?

options.text: Whether the named method is declared as static or as an instance method
options.says: The page's key question is whether the referenced method is static or an instance method, checked in the class's declaration.

options.text: Whether the class name is written with its package or without its package
options.says: The page never ties the kind to how the class is named; it looks only at the method's declaration.

options.text: Whether the reference is written inside a static method or an instance one
options.says: Where the reference is written does not matter; the page asks whether the referenced method itself is static.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, where can a constructor reference to a class's private constructor be used?

options.text: Anywhere at all, since a reference skips the access check that new makes
options.says: The page says the same access rules as new apply.

options.text: Only in a subclass, since a reference widens private access to protected
options.says: The page says nothing widens: the same access rules as new apply.

options.text: Only where that constructor is accessible, as with an ordinary new
options.says: The page answers that the reference works only where the constructor is accessible, such as inside the class itself.

concepts: A constructor reference obeys the same access rules as new.
ClassName::method is a static or an unbound reference according to how the method is declared.
